from: docs/design/redesign/07-balance-lab.md section 3.2 (variants at four depths, rule slots with contracts, file overlays, no runtime switch) and the phase table row '3. Variants'; families from docs/design/redesign/04-math-strategy.md
format: A SLOT is one module of the tree with a narrow contract. `rule`: the exports a family replaces; every other export a family must take from the shipped module (export * from './<name>.shipped.js', which a scratch copy keeps beside the overlay). `offPath`: shipped exports that call a rule export but never run in a hunt, each with why. `contract`: what the slot promises, each line an id that tools/balance-program/slot-contracts.mjs checks, plus the GENERIC lines every slot carries. `formula`: the slot's row in formulas/formulas-architecture.json, whose typed reads and writes the model graph holds (no second copy here).

A FAMILY is a whole replacement file on the shelf, its path DERIVED from its slot and id (tools/balance-program/variants/<slot>/<slot>.<family>.js, a basename unique in the repository), first line `// balance-variant: <slot>/<family>`. kind: 'shipped' (the tree's own module, no file), 'identity' (a copy overlay: it must play byte-identical), 'formula' (a rival family, named from 04-math-strategy.md). A formula family carries `added` and `expires`: the winner moves into the tree, the loser is deleted, and tests/rule-slots.mjs is red on a family past its date (read against the commit's own date, so one commit always reads the same).

status 'cut': the slot is one module with a contract and plays depth 3 overlays. status 'git-ref': the seam is not cut; a family of it is depth 4, a candidate that names an engine branch (`base: { ref }`), with `seam` saying what cutting it takes and `why` it is not cut here.

slots.label: What armor does to a landed blow

contract.says: mitigationOf answers whole dodgePm, absorbPm and keepPm in 0..1000 and a whole ward of 0 or more, for armor values 0 to 10^6 against attackers of Level 1 to 100,000; NO_MITIGATION is all zeros
with no armor of any weight a blow lands as the resistance leaves it: max(1, floor(n x el / 1000))
armor never adds damage: a landed blow is a whole number from 1 to max(1, floor(n x el / 1000))
more heavy or light armor never lands more on a blow; more medium never lands more in expectation (dodge included, within one point and a permille of the blow: the whole-permille cap)
a bigger blow never lands less
an attacker of a higher Level never lands less in expectation (dodge included, within one point and a permille of the blow)
with no Tempering the chain draws nothing from the dice, so every family plays the shipped draw order
the same armor, Level and blow give the same answer

families.what: Armor against the attacker's Level, capped: maxPm x P / (P + k x the attacker's Level) for dodge and absorb, a flat ward, and a total cap of 60%
families.source: 04-math-strategy.md section 2 'Armor against the attacker's Level, with a cap' (today's family; section 15 'Defense, the alternative')

families.what: the shipped module through the overlay, unchanged
Armor against hit size, uncapped: heavy absorb = maxPm x P / (P + 0.5 x the blow), set to agree with the shipped line on an average blow
families.source: 04-math-strategy.md section 2 'Armor against hit size' and section 15 'Defense'

slots.label: How a kill's Level XP is shared by a party

offPath.partyVsAlone: the Party window's measured line (src/shell): read by the page, never by the engine
offPath.partyBestLine: the Hunts window's party advice (src/shell/hunt-list.js): read by the page, never by the engine

contract.says: partyClassXp answers a whole permille above 0 and a list of classes, for parties of 0 to 100 heroes and roles it does not know
the classes a party holds are the shipped reading's: a family changes the pay, never the classes
the order of the heroes never changes the pay
at one size, a party holding more classes is never paid less
the same heroes give the same answer

families.what: The class table: a factor on the even share by party size and classes held, +15% for a hero alone
the shipped module through the overlay, unchanged
No party table: an even share at partyPay 1.0 for every party, no boost alone

contract.says: deathXpLoss answers whole losses above 0 keyed by level or a combat skill (zeros omitted), for heroes of Level 1 to 100,000
a death never takes more Level XP than the hero holds (Level 1 is the floor)
a combat skill loses at most its progress into its level, never a level
a share of 0 (a mode that prices nothing) takes nothing
a larger share never takes less
more Level XP never loses less Level XP
deathXpLoss's Level loss is levelDeathLoss's: one price, every reader
the same hero gives the same answer

families.what: 6% of ALL Level XP and 6% of each combat skill's progress, times the session mode's share
the shipped module through the overlay, unchanged
Hours of progress: 7.5 hours of the pace contract at the hero's Level (parity with 6% at Level 60), never below Level 1

slots.label: A hero's power as two ratios: what its blows gain and what its taken blows lose
slots.why: lane/r4 (2026-11-22): cut at temper.js, not combat.js. The blow line in combat.js is R2's seam (a whole-file family would race it); temper.js answers the two per-hero permilles every amount passes (damage.js hurt, abilities.js, mitigation.js mitigate), so a geometric power step plays as a ratio on them with no combat code changed. The skill part (weightSkill) needs member.js, R9's lane

contract.says: blowsPmOf answers a whole permille of 0 or more and armorPmOf a whole permille from 0 to 999, for every weapon and armor set of the catalogue with and without Tempering
a hero wearing nothing gains nothing and loses nothing, Tempered or not
with no Tempering, a weapon (an armor set) of a higher item Level never answers a smaller blowsPm (armorPm)
the same kit and Tempering give the same answer

families.what: Tempering only: the weapon's Blows rung and the worn armor's Armor rungs, at their ladders' permille; nothing from gear itself
the shipped module through the overlay, unchanged

The power step on gear: blows gain (1 + powerStep)^(weightGear x the weapon's item Level) and taken blows lose (1 + powerStep)^(weightGear x the armor's mean item Level), on top of Tempering; weightGear 1.0 as a measuring value
families.source: 04-math-strategy.md section 1 'What a hero's rating is made of' and section 2 'The step contest'
